statement: Let S(root) be the multiset of sizes of all perfect binary subtrees of root, counted one entry per node occurrence: a perfect binary subtree is a node occurrence u together with all descendants of u such that the resulting tree is perfect (all leaves are at the same level and every non-leaf node has exactly two children), and its size is its number of nodes. Let A be the list of elements of S(root) sorted in non-increasing order, with duplicates preserved. The function returns a result r (it does not fail), and: if len(A) < k then r = -1; if len(A) >= k then r = A[k-1] (using 1-based k, so A[0] is the largest and A[k-1] is the kth largest).
preconditions: root is a Tree with N node occurrences, 1 <= N <= 2000; every Node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2000; k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= 1024.

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail) for every input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: root is a Tree with N node occurrences, 1 <= N <= 2000; every Node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2000; k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= 1024.

statement: Let N be the number of node occurrences in root. Whenever the function returns a result r, either r = -1 or 1 <= r <= N.
preconditions: root is a Tree with N node occurrences, 1 <= N <= 2000; every Node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2000; k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= 1024.

statement: Let C be the number of node occurrences u in root such that the subtree rooted at u is a perfect binary tree (all leaves at the same level, every internal node has two children). The function returns a result r, and r = -1 if and only if k > C.
preconditions: root is a Tree with N node occurrences, 1 <= N <= 2000; every Node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2000; k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= 1024.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, there exists a node occurrence u in root such that the subtree rooted at u is a perfect binary tree (all leaves at the same level, every internal node has two children) and has exactly r nodes.
preconditions: root is a Tree with N node occurrences, 1 <= N <= 2000; every Node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2000; k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= 1024.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, the number of perfect binary subtrees of root whose size is strictly greater than r is at most k-1, and the number of perfect binary subtrees of root whose size is at least r is at least k.
preconditions: root is a Tree with N node occurrences, 1 <= N <= 2000; every Node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2000; k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= 1024.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r is the maximum element of the multiset S(root) of sizes of all perfect binary subtrees of root: there is a perfect binary subtree of size r, and every perfect binary subtree of root has size at most r.
preconditions: root is a Tree with N node occurrences, 1 <= N <= 2000; every Node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2000; k = 1.

statement: Let N be the number of node occurrences in root. The function returns a result r and r = N.
preconditions: root is a Tree with N node occurrences, 1 <= N <= 2000; every Node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2000; k = 1; root itself is a perfect binary tree.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, there exists an integer h >= 1 such that r = 2^h - 1. Equivalently, r is positive and r+1 is a power of two.
preconditions: root is a Tree with N node occurrences, 1 <= N <= 2000; every Node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2000; k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= 1024.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = 1.
preconditions: root is a Tree with N node occurrences, 1 <= N <= 2000; every Node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2000; let C be the number of perfect binary subtrees of root; assume C <= 1024 and k = C.

statement: Let r1 be the result of the function on (root, k1) and r2 the result on (root, k2). The function returns both results, and r1 >= r2.
preconditions: root is a Tree with N node occurrences, 1 <= N <= 2000; every Node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2000; k1 and k2 are i64 values with 1 <= k1 <= k2 <= 1024.

statement: Let r1 be the result on (root1, k) and r2 the result on (root2, k). The function returns both results, and r1 = r2.
preconditions: root1 and root2 are Trees with the same shape (one is obtained from the other by changing only the i64 values at Node constructors, leaving all Null/Node positions and left/right child links unchanged); each has N node occurrences with 1 <= N <= 2000; every Node value in each tree satisfies 1 <= v <= 2000; k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= 1024.

statement: Let N be the number of node occurrences in root. Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, r < N.
preconditions: root is a Tree with N node occurrences, 1 <= N <= 2000; every Node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2000; k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= 1024; root itself is not a perfect binary tree.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = 1 if k = 1, while r = -1 if k > 1.
preconditions: root is exactly Node(v, Null, Null) for some i64 v with 1 <= v <= 2000; k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= 1024.

statement: Let H be the height of root measured in nodes (a Null tree has height 0 and a Node has height 1 plus the maximum height of its children). Whenever the function returns a result r with r != -1, r <= 2^H - 1.
preconditions: root is a Tree with N node occurrences, 1 <= N <= 2000; every Node value v satisfies 1 <= v <= 2000; k is an i64 with 1 <= k <= 1024.
